How could a show about such an outsize hero as Hercules be so lame? That’s the question hovering over a Disney-backed musical that arrived at the Theater Royal, Drury Lane, in London on Tuesday, just nine months after the playhouse waved goodbye to “Frozen,” another screen-to-stage cull from the Disney catalog.
Simba's underpowered sibling needs to go back to the gym and bulk up.
But there's no doubt this feel-good family show will delight Drury Lane's youngest audience members.
The rest of us are more likely to find ourselves craving a scintilla of nuance, a whiff of real jeopardy – any reason at all, really, to care about the antics on stage.
Hercules is antiseptic fun, carefully manufactured. It isn't a bad night out, but it's like a fizzy drink, lively on the tongue but ultimately unsatisfying.
Unfortunately, there's none of the same imaginative energy in this stodgy new stage version.
Hercules, though, is one unit of generic Disney stage entertainment.
Hercules is a heroic hit, complete with tunics, thunderbolts, and toe-tapping tunes.
